name: Chip supply
value: TSMC halts some China orders at 16nm and below
summary: US rules from 19 Nov led TSMC to halt some Chinese orders at 16nm and below; AI demand strains auto chip supply
state: US Commerce Department rules effective 19 Nov closed a route that let some Chinese chip designers obtain advanced manufacturing without licences; TSMC has halted affected orders at 16nm and below unless customers get US licences (The Standard, 19 Nov; Taipei Times, 20 Nov). Chipmakers warned on 10 Nov that AI demand is creating bottlenecks in automotive supply chains (The Star). No new controls or fab outage were found by 25 Nov; new controls keep Watch, and TSMC and Samsung output itself is not disrupted.
for_you: Little immediate effect on UK consumers. Carmakers and electronics firms relying on mature or memory chips are most exposed to longer lead times and higher component costs.
rubric_hit: Watch: new export controls (US rules effective 19 Nov) and shortages in key segments; no major TSMC/Samsung output disruption

sources.title: The Standard — TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
